parsed.explanation: The combined regime's worst feature is a state-level universal-exposure measure: a February 2026 law confining trans people to birth-sex facilities in all publicly owned buildings — expressly including airports — with civil and criminal penalties up to $1,000 and bounty suits of at least $1,000 by any private person, applying to visitors passing through. Layered on that is federal entry screening that refuses cases where documents cast doubt on sex, with a possible lifetime fraud finding, and documented abuse of trans people in immigration custody. There is no general criminalisation of trans identity, state anti-discrimination law exists, and courts function, but the courts have enforced the hostile ID rules rather than relieved them, and the facility law's challenge has produced no injunction. Absence of documented street-violence data gives no safety credit.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal cable directs refusal where documents/records cast doubt on sex, with possible permanent fraud ineligibility; trans athletes barred; reports of passports blocked and detentions of neighbouring citizens over visas; eight governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; passport policy under litigation; fraud finding requires all four elements and is never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: A marker/presentation mismatch at the consular or port stage can cascade into refusal, a permanent ineligibility finding, or immigration detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans men in immigration custody reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; federal prisons apply conversion-therapy-style policies, deny care, and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts; state facility law carries criminal penalty and an arrest precedent held 24 hours in a men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Limited waiver possibilities on fraud findings; no documented custody protocol congruent with gender identity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border document dispute converts a visitor into a detainee held under the practices above.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State law confines trans people to birth-sex facilities in all publicly owned buildings including airports, universities and government offices, with civil/criminal penalties up to $1,000 and private bounty suits of at least $1,000; federal order bars gender-congruent access to federally funded single-sex facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State public-accommodations law has covered gender identity since 2020; a challenge by two trans men was filed within days.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The bounty mechanism needs no prosecutor: any private person in an airport or government building can sue a trans visitor directly, and no injunction is recorded.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for minors under 18 (enforcement enjoined May 2026); federal orders frame minor care as mutilation and target reimbursement; no documented emergency-care denial to visitors.
care_services.protection: Adult care is not banned in the state; a district-court injunction blocks the minor ban in a parental lawsuit.
care_services.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor cannot rely on the state's care system; a visitor's own HRT supply is a border-screening risk rather than a state-law issue.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'rapid identification and neutralization' of groups described as 'radically pro-transgender'; a December 2025 reward memorandum invokes 'radical gender ideology'; an executive order directs investigation of schools and prosecution of teachers affirming trans minors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; 'radical gender ideology' is not a reward criterion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing raises the chance that an outed visitor attracts hostile official attention rather than neutral processing.

minors_guardians.exposure: The facility/bounty law reaches minors in public buildings including airports, exposing accompanying guardians to suits; federal order contemplates criminal prosecution of adults who affirm a minor's transition.
minors_guardians.protection: The minor care ban is enjoined; a parental lawsuit is active.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces both the facility exposure and a state that frames affirmation as harm.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence rate or pattern is documented for this jurisdiction; the state hate-crime statute covers sexual orientation but not gender identity; 66% of polled residents back birth-sex document rules.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime law has covered gender identity since 2009; state law prohibits gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Where state bias-crime law omits gender identity, recourse depends on federal charging, which the dossier does not document in practice.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: The facility law's challenge has produced no ruling or injunction; the highest court refused appeal in the ID case, letting marker invalidation continue; bounty-suit and enforcement counts are unrecorded.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation is pending; a legal-aid FAQ covers document rules; federal anti-discrimination and hate-crime statutes exist on paper.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Courts have functioned to enforce the hostile document rule, so institutional efficacy here is exposure, not recourse.

anchor_checks.comparison: Materially safer. The 0.15 anchor makes severe multi-year imprisonment the standard outcome after discovery, with capital exposure in the background. Here no statute criminalises trans identity as such, no prosecution for being trans is documented, and the criminal exposure is a fine-level facility offence, not imprisonment as the norm.

Somewhat worse overall. The 0.25 anchor produces invasive review, document confiscation and denial of entry without detention or penalty. Here border refusal plus possible lifetime ineligibility is comparable, but added is a universal facility ban with private bounty suits in airports and documented abuse in immigration custody — offset partly by no arbitrary extortion and a functioning (if hostile-leaning) legal order.

Worse. The 0.35 anchor ends in release with a helpline and a charter barring prolonged holds, the discrepancy merely logged. Here the equivalent mismatch can yield refusal with a permanent fraud finding, and the state's bounty provision gives every bystander standing to sue a trans visitor in a public building.

Considerably worse. The 0.45 anchor involves a refusal of a dormitory bed and civil mediation with no detention. Here the facility exclusion is statutory, penalty-bearing and privately enforceable, with a documented arrest precedent and misgendered custody.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a hostile state facility-and-identification statute sitting inside a hostile federal document and custody regime. The heaviest input is traveller-facing and near-unavoidable: an outed trans visitor using a restroom in an airport or government building in this state is exposed to a private bounty suit and a penalty up to $1,000, with no recorded injunction. Entry screening compounds this — document doubt can mean refusal and a possible lifetime ineligibility finding — and detention would place the visitor in federally documented abusive custody. Countervailing: no criminalisation of trans identity, an operating state anti-discrimination law, a federal gender-identity hate-crime statute, and pending litigation. But courts have so far enforced the hostile rules rather than relieved them, and no violence data exists to credit. This sits in the High Risk band, above the worst imprisonment regimes, below jurisdictions where only paperwork friction applies.
